name: AIS 2024 RTSR Challenge (Real-Time 4K Super-Resolution of AVIF)
description: This paper introduces a novel benchmark as part of the AIS 2024 Real-Time Image Super-Resolution (RTSR) Challenge, which aims to upscale compressed images from 540p to 4K resolution (4x factor) in real-time on commercial GPUs. For this, we use a diverse test set containing a variety of 4K images ranging from digital art to gaming and photography. The images are compressed using the modern AVIF codec, instead of JPEG. All the proposed methods improve PSNR fidelity over Lanczos interpolation, and process images under 10ms. Out of the 160 participants, 25 teams submitted their code and models. The solutions present novel designs tailored for memory-efficiency and runtime on edge devices. This survey describes the best solutions for real-time SR of compressed high-resolution images.
evaluation_method: PSNR/SSIM for fidelity plus runtime (inference latency) and memory footprint for real-time constraints
general_score_metric: PSNR (primary), with SSIM and runtime/latency constraints reported
typical_sota_score: 30–38 dB PSNR (varies by content and compression level)
reputation: Well-regarded within the real-time image super-resolution and vision-efficiency community for its focus on AVIF-compressed 4K and practical runtime targets.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; results are hardware- and implementation-dependent; uses AVIF compression which may limit direct comparability to JPEG-focused SR benchmarks; competitive/small test set from the challenge.
